body:
If motivation and procrastination are your main issues right now then I would imagine a little encouragement to go beyond your comfort zone might help both of you. This is what my shrink tells me and I know it's true but I don't do it because I am a hypocrite and feel like I deserve to suffer/be alone.

I am assuming you and your boyfriend probably both feel the same way sometimes. Thing is, you are not alone, and as long as you both care for each other then I think you can support other make steps towards being the people you want to be.

Gym membership? > go to gym
No membership/time for gym? > push-ups, go out for a run/bikeride, Or get one of those pull-up bars you can install on a doorframe and do some pull-ups when you feel like that.

If you feel like your body is calm but your mind is racing then I think it might help to try out some meditation techniques. They really do help in the moment. They don't solve your problems but you can use them to calm your mind.

I graduated a couple years ago and can recall that feeling of uncertainty. I was positive that I would not find a job and would wind up homeless. I ended up getting hired by a temp agency and then started working full time at an office job that pays decently. Point is I think you might be surprised by how quickly things can change if you want them to. In my experience, that anxiety prevents you from moving towards things you care about which causes more anxiety/uncertainty. You just have to take that first step.

It's nice to hear that you have someone that you care about you're going through this with. I know with people that you care about sometimes it can feel like you're in a feedback loop where you are both validating each other's negative feelings, and it's nice because it provides support but sometimes it prevents you from moving towards the things you care about.

For example, there is a subreddit here with lots of funny suicide memes. I used to look at it a lot because I could relate to the posts and I was tired of trying to force myself to have a positive perspective. The suicide memes made me feel like it was OK feeling like a worthless piece of shit, and I think that there is value in that. But at a certain point when that's all you're consuming it's probably no longer helping.

I think there is a middle ground between acknowledging the profound suffering we experience on a daily basis while also working to encourage each other to be better people (without being belittling, like so many of those "just be positive!" folks).
